messages.content: Be an adversarial ICLR reviewer. Evaluate one possible pivot for a world-model security paper: “predictive-authority inversion” — when an action-conditioned world model is updated from truthful interactive experience, its forecast of an unobserved or partially observed state can acquire more decision authority than a fresh private measurement; a forecast-assisted actor then skips/discounts verification, and the resulting action makes the forecast self-confirming. The attacker only executes legal actions and contributes authentic observations/rewards; no fake labels, prompts, weights, or planner writes. Existing evidence in our ScienceWorld native system: (1) truthful bypass-circuit memories change lamp-status prediction; a hybrid Qwen world-model + official Gemini actor had clean=100, benign=100, bypass=-100 once, with bypass actor skipping measurement after an imagined bulb-on forecast; but task-level attack loss is one instance and later task swaps/real measurements often repair it. (2) truthful overheat curriculum changes thermometer forecast 116C→187C, but hybrid actor still succeeds 100, only with extra actions. (3) five corrective users do not change retrieval, while researcher-only recency intervention repairs prediction. Existing reviews call measurement substitution/provenance/retrieval capture generic or unproven. Decide if a broad one-sentence claim can reach novelty 7-7.5 after proper controls, or REJECT. If viable, give an exact 2-minute native gate with multiple core tasks, strong baselines, causal intervention and closest primary prior art. Do not treat the numbers above as proof of novelty.

{"request": ["Return strict JSON: decision, novelty_score, overlap_risks, missing_causal_step, one_sentence_claim_if_viable, gate, controls, defense, scale_conditions. Be conservative.", "Compare against world-model security lifecycle, BadWAM, TRAP, CoCo, OneWorld, OEP/MINJA, active-learning poisoning, forecast-assisted decision making, and sensor/measurement verification prior art."]}
